title: Boundary reflection and compressed wavefronts
reviewed_arguments: Local smooth scalar second order, real principal symbol, arbitrary complex lower terms and noncharacteristic boundary are retained. No global time or Lorentz signature is assumed.
The transverse Hamilton base map and explicit canonical pairing calculation RFA1 prove normal coordinates even when the full principal quadratic form is degenerate.
Both roots, normal velocities, the sign of the r-parameter Hamilton flow and invariant root interchange are checked. Physical time and Hamilton parameter have distinct orientations in the flat model.
Compression uses r rho. Intrinsic normal derivatives, the ambient delta correction and actual trace agreement use the complete EW and BW proofs.

EW proves the full elliptic identity, including rough initial data, redundant measurements, the actual compact auxiliary problem and full lower-order comparison. The scalar stable Dirichlet evaluation equals one.

Both ordered scalar factorizations are separately constructed. RFA2 cancels every positive normal derivative exactly; the full Riccati recursion retains noncommuting factors, every normal-parameter derivative and Borel remainders.

The two commuting tests have one identical full initial operator. Proper kernel support, a fixed compact transported cone and the common N-domain collar give smooth forcing in all global Sobolev orders for the localized Cauchy problems.

At a fixed positive interior slice, characteristic graph control and first-order ellipticity exclude every normal lift. The full HC slice theorem proves an actually smooth datum, not merely one regular covector.
Backward and forward smooth Cauchy solutions are identified with the distributional tested solutions using the complete HC uniqueness proof, including the Schwartz adjoint and all weighted moments.

Exact boundary comparison transfers smooth initial data between the two ordered systems. Separate parametrices recover their two first-order actions on u; subtraction cancels D_r, and the elliptic root difference recovers u.

Reflection holds in both directions. Interior real-principal propagation, including radial and stationary cases, yields all-or-none propagation on source-free connected intervals with locally finite transverse reflections.
The flat reflected delta wave is verified by localization, the exact tensor theorem and cotangent pullback. Its intrinsic normal trace is 2i delta-prime.

The flat coefficient example is in N by the actual compressed left quantization RFA3: cone volume and arbitrary Fourier decay bound every ordinary derivative uniformly at the boundary. Full lacunary and residual terms are retained.

All four original complete solutions, all forty-three original displays and the exact coordinate figure are preserved. Their mixed-quadratic, anisotropic, elliptic Poisson and repeated-reflection calculations were checked.
